title: The Great Pyramid
topic: How the Great Pyramid of Khufu was built
script:
On the Giza plateau, west of the Nile, stands the last surviving wonder of the ancient world.

It was built for King Khufu of the Fourth Dynasty, more than four thousand five hundred years ago.

Fine white limestone for its casing was quarried at Tura and carried across the Nile by boat.

Papyrus logbooks found at Wadi al-Jarf record one crew's journeys with that stone.

Evidence from a workers' town nearby suggests the builders were organised labourers who were housed and fed, not slaves.

Crews hauled an estimated two million blocks into place, course upon course.

Deep inside, narrow passages lead to the King's Chamber and its granite sarcophagus.

When it was finished, it rose about one hundred and forty-six metres, and for nearly four thousand years nothing built by human hands stood taller.
